evidence: app/app/abilities/[name]/page.tsx:1 — entire feature lives in one route directory; imports only shared generic helpers
app/app/pokemon/[name]/page.tsx:117 — the only inbound link is the Abilities section on the Pokémon page (spec-mandated), so removal means one localized edit there
app/app/layout.tsx:26 — nav links only Pokémon and Types; no ability references in shared chrome
app/lib/api.ts:136 — Ability type in api.ts would linger as dead code, and .card__note CSS (app/app/globals.css:254) only serves the ability hidden-note
removability.rationale: The feature is self-contained in one directory with no dedicated shared code; the only extra edits are the spec-mandated cross-links on the Pokémon page plus minor dead-code cleanup (Ability type, card__note CSS).

evidence: app/lib/data.ts:55-76 — cardsForPokemon builds cards for move/ability/type lists
app/app/page.tsx:33-39 — home page re-implements card construction inline instead of reusing cardsForPokemon, so a sprite/name fix lands twice
app/lib/data.ts:21-23 — spriteUrl derives sprites by ID convention, while app/app/pokemon/[name]/page.tsx:54 uses API-provided sprites on the detail page — two sources of truth for 'the right sprite'

app/components/Filters.tsx:13-20 — client href builder duplicates the omit-defaults query rule that app/app/page.tsx:41-50 (pageHref) and :22-28 (parsing) also encode; adding/renaming a filter param touches both files in sync
changeability.rationale: Most fixes are findable but not one-place: card-building and query-param knowledge are each duplicated across two files, so the Deoxys-style sprite fix and any filter change land in 2–3 coordinated places.

evidence: app/lib/api.ts:1 and app/lib/data.ts:1 — import "server-only" enforces the server/client boundary at module level
app/components/MoveTable.tsx:8-19 — client component receives a narrow, serializable MoveRow prop; no API knowledge leaks in
app/components/PokemonCards.tsx:5 — takes plain CardData, shared by four routes without depending on any page

app/app/pokemon/[name]/page.tsx:178 — getMoves orchestration (version-group ordering constants at :30, :37) lives inside the page file rather than the data layer, making the biggest page also own data-shaping policy
coupling.rationale: Loosely coupled with clear seams — all HTTP goes through lib/api, all card logic through lib/data, client components are leaf and prop-driven. The only tangle is the Pokémon page file doing its own move-table data orchestration.

evidence: app/lib/data.ts:55-75 — cardsForPokemon is generic over the entry shape with an extra() callback, absorbing the real variation (hidden-ability note at app/app/abilities/[name]/page.tsx:24) without flags
app/components/Section.tsx:17 — Section handles titled-region markup once for every page
app/components/TypeBadge.tsx:8 — link/size flags map to genuine variation (linked vs plain, card vs summary size)

app/app/moves/[name]/page.tsx:10-19, app/app/abilities/[name]/page.tsx:11-20, app/app/types/[name]/page.tsx:31-40 — the getX + generateMetadata + notFound boilerplate is copy-pasted per resource; an Items route would copy it a fourth time
app/lib/format.ts:7-30 — formatting rules (humanize, english, orMissing, latestFlavorText) extracted around the spec's actual definitions, reused everywhere
abstraction_design.rationale: The data and component abstractions stretch to new cases without flags (the extra() seam is well judged), but the resource-page skeleton is duplicated rather than factored, so a new resource type repeats ~20 lines of boilerplate per page.

findings.issue: Home page re-implements card construction (sprite URL, label, types) instead of reusing cardsForPokemon, so any card fix must land in two places
findings.suggestion: Have the home page build CardData via a shared builder (or make getSpeciesIndex emit CardData-ready rows) so all four card lists share one construction path

findings.issue: Query-param knowledge (names, defaults, omit-empty rule) is duplicated between the client href builder and the server's parse + pageHref; adding a filter requires synchronized edits
findings.suggestion: Extract a single buildQuery(state, page?) helper in lib (no server-only import) used by both Filters.tsx and page.tsx

findings.issue: Sprites are derived by URL convention while the detail page uses API-provided sprite fields (app/app/pokemon/[name]/page.tsx:54), creating two sources of truth for sprite selection
findings.suggestion: Centralize sprite selection in lib/data.ts (species → default variety) and have cards consume it, so the Deoxys-type fix is one change

findings.issue: The 260-line Pokémon page mixes presentation with the getMoves data orchestration (method ordering constants, version-group sorting)
findings.suggestion: Move getMoves into lib/data.ts alongside cardsForPokemon/getSpeciesIndex, keeping the page compositional like the other three resource pages

findings.issue: The getX + generateMetadata + notFound boilerplate is copy-pasted in all four resource pages; an Items route would copy it again
findings.suggestion: Add a small helper (e.g. resourcePage(fetch, formatTitle)) shared by resource routes, or accept the duplication consciously — it is the framework's per-route shape

findings.issue: export const dynamic = "force-dynamic" plus a hand-rolled TTL cache (app/lib/api.ts:7-34) is the legacy model; Next.js 16.4 recommends Cache Components and removes `dynamic` when it's enabled (default in 17)
findings.suggestion: Plan the migration: replace the manual cache with `use cache`/cacheLife and drop the route-segment config; today's single-place caching rules make that a contained change

summary: A well-structured App Router codebase: server-only data modules with narrow interfaces, generic seams (cardsForPokemon's extra callback, Section, TypeBadge) that absorb real variation, and a single apiBase for the data source. The main editability costs are duplicated card construction (home page vs cardsForPokemon) and query-param knowledge split between server and client, which make the sprite-class and filter-class fixes two-place changes. Everything else — removal, data-source swap, a new Items route — is close to best case, and the code sits on the current stable Next 16.4.3, with only the legacy caching model flagged for the upcoming 17 migration.
